_meta.derivation: DERIVED from the WCAG 2.2 Recommendation, NOT transcribed from PRD §14. The PRD names 20 plans but does not enumerate them in this repository; presenting an invented list as §14's would be a fabricated citation in a compliance feature (PRD §19). Replace this file to adopt the real §14 catalog — no code reads the plan text.
_meta.why_every_criterion_has_a_plan: axe-core publishes rules for 23 of these 55 criteria; 32 have none at all. The 23 do not get a pass either: every acr_axe row declares Coverage.PARTIAL and CAN_CERTIFY_PASS is {FULL} (ADR 0031), so automation finishes no criterion and every applicable one needs a human.

plans.title: Keyboard operability sweep
plans.why_manual: axe can see that a control is focusable; it cannot operate it. Whether every function is REACHABLE and USABLE by keyboard, and whether focus can always be moved away again, is only established by a person driving the interface.
preconditions: Unplug or ignore the mouse for the whole session. Reaching for it invalidates the run.
Start from the application's entry screen, signed in as an ordinary user.

steps.action: Tab forward through the entire screen, then Shift+Tab back to the start.
steps.expect: Every interactive control is reachable in both directions, and focus never enters a component it cannot leave by Tab, Shift+Tab or Escape (2.1.2).

steps.action: Operate each control from the keyboard — Enter/Space on buttons, arrows in menus, listboxes, tabs and sliders.
steps.expect: Every function available by pointer is available from the keyboard (2.1.1).

steps.action: Open every dialog, menu and popover, then dismiss each with Escape.
steps.expect: Focus returns to the control that opened it, and no dialog traps focus.

steps.action: Press each single-character key (letters, digits, punctuation) with no modifier while focus is on the page body rather than a text field.
steps.expect: Either nothing happens, or any single-key shortcut can be turned off, remapped, or is active only while a component has focus (2.1.4).

plans.title: Focus visibility, order and obscuring
plans.why_manual: axe-core has NO rule for any of these three. Whether a focus indicator is actually visible, whether the order preserves meaning, and whether a sticky header hides the focused control are all visual judgements about a rendered page.
preconditions: Use a real browser at default zoom. jsdom has no layout engine and cannot answer any of this.

steps.action: Tab through the screen watching only the focus indicator.
steps.expect: The focused control is visibly indicated at every step, with no point where focus is invisible (2.4.7).

steps.action: Compare the tab order against the visual reading order of the screen.
steps.expect: Focus moves in an order that preserves meaning and operability (2.4.3).

steps.action: Scroll so a sticky header, footer or floating panel overlaps content, then Tab to controls beneath it.
steps.expect: No focused control is entirely hidden by author-created content (2.4.11).

steps.action: Open each modal and Tab through it.
steps.expect: Focus is placed in the dialog on open and confined to it while it is open.

plans.title: Screen reader: page structure and relationships
plans.why_manual: axe checks that heading and landmark MARKUP is well formed. It cannot judge whether the structure conveyed matches the structure a sighted user perceives, whether the reading sequence preserves meaning, or whether a heading actually describes its section.
preconditions: Use a screen reader you can name and version — NVDA, JAWS or VoiceOver.
Record the exact browser + screen reader pairing; results are not portable between them.

steps.action: List the headings with the screen reader's heading list.
steps.expect: Headings describe their sections and nest without skipping a level (2.4.6).

steps.action: List the landmarks and regions.
steps.expect: Each region is identified, and a mechanism exists to skip repeated blocks of content (2.4.1).

steps.action: Read the screen top to bottom in browse mode.
steps.expect: The reading sequence conveys the same meaning as the visual order (1.3.2).

steps.action: Enter each table and each form group and read its relationships.
steps.expect: Header cells, groups and labels are programmatically associated with what they describe (1.3.1).

plans.title: Screen reader: name, role and value of every control
plans.why_manual: axe can detect a control with NO accessible name. It cannot tell whether the name is the right one, whether it contains the visible label text, or whether an instruction is sufficient to complete the field.
preconditions: Have the visible screen in front of you while listening.

steps.action: Move to every control and compare what is announced with what is displayed.
steps.expect: Name, role and current value are announced, and the announced name contains the visible label text (4.1.2, 2.5.3).

steps.action: Change the state of every toggle, checkbox, expandable and tab.
steps.expect: The new state is announced without needing to re-read the page.

steps.action: Enter each form field cold, without reading the screen first.
steps.expect: The label and any required format instruction are announced, and are enough to complete the field correctly (3.3.2).

plans.title: Status messages announced without focus movement
plans.why_manual: axe has NO rule for 4.1.3. Whether a status message is actually announced, and announced without stealing focus, can only be heard.
preconditions: Screen reader running with default verbosity.

steps.action: Trigger each success, error, progress and result-count message without moving focus to it.
steps.expect: Each is announced by the screen reader (4.1.3).

steps.action: Watch where focus is while each message appears.
steps.expect: Focus is not moved to the message; the user's place is preserved.

steps.action: Trigger a long-running operation.
steps.expect: Progress and completion are announced, not only shown.

plans.title: Text alternatives convey equivalent purpose
plans.why_manual: axe detects a MISSING alt attribute. Whether the alternative conveys the same purpose as the image — and whether a decorative image is correctly hidden rather than described — is a judgement about meaning that no tool makes.
preconditions: Inventory every non-text element: images, icons, charts, canvases, media thumbnails, CSS background images that carry meaning.

steps.action: For each informative image, read its alternative with the image hidden.
steps.expect: The alternative serves the same purpose as the image (1.1.1).

steps.action: For each decorative image, check how it is exposed.
steps.expect: It is hidden from assistive technology rather than given a description.

steps.action: For each chart or data visualisation, look for the equivalent.
steps.expect: The information is available in text or a table, not only as a picture.

steps.action: For each icon-only control, listen to its announced name.
steps.expect: The name describes the ACTION, not the glyph.

plans.title: Prerecorded audio and video alternatives
plans.why_manual: This is the criterion group where automation is most dangerously misleading. A page with no <video> makes axe report `inapplicable`, which says NOTHING about whether the product captions its videos — see api/acr_axe.py. Only an inventory of the product's actual media answers it.
preconditions: Build an inventory of EVERY prerecorded audio and video asset the product presents, including onboarding, help, marketing and embedded third-party media.
If the inventory is genuinely empty, that is a Not Applicable decision with an explanation — not a pass, and not a skipped plan.

steps.action: For each audio-only and video-only asset, look for the alternative.
steps.expect: An equivalent text alternative is available, or an audio track for video-only content (1.2.1).

steps.action: Play each video with sound and read the captions.
steps.expect: Captions are present, synchronised, and include speaker identification and meaningful non-speech audio (1.2.2).

steps.action: Watch each video with the screen off, listening only.
steps.expect: An audio description or a full text alternative conveys the visual information (1.2.3, 1.2.5).

plans.title: Live media captions
plans.why_manual: Live content cannot be tested from a static page at all.
preconditions: Identify any live audio the product streams — webinars, live support, broadcast.
If there is none, that is a Not Applicable decision with an explanation.

steps.action: Join a live session and enable captions.
steps.expect: Real-time captions are available for live audio content (1.2.4).

steps.action: Follow the captions for several minutes against the spoken audio.
steps.expect: Captions keep pace and are accurate enough to follow the content.

plans.title: Colour and sensory characteristics are never the only cue
plans.why_manual: axe cannot tell whether colour is the ONLY means of conveying something. That requires understanding what the interface is trying to communicate.
preconditions: Have a greyscale filter available (OS display filter or browser devtools).

steps.action: View every screen in greyscale.
steps.expect: Every distinction still readable — status, validity, required-ness, selection, chart series — is conveyed by more than colour (1.4.1).

steps.action: Read every instruction in the interface.
steps.expect: No instruction depends solely on shape, size, position, orientation or sound — 'the button on the right', 'the round icon' (1.3.3).

steps.action: Check links within blocks of text.
steps.expect: Links are distinguishable from surrounding text without relying on colour.

plans.title: Text and non-text contrast, measured
plans.why_manual: axe DOES check text contrast, and reports `incomplete` — not a pass — whenever it cannot resolve a background: over an image, a gradient, or a partially transparent layer. Those are exactly the cases a person must measure. 1.4.11 has no axe rule.
preconditions: Use a contrast measurement tool that samples rendered pixels.
Test in BOTH light and dark themes. A fix in one can break the other.

steps.action: Measure every case axe reported as `incomplete`.
steps.expect: Text meets 4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text (1.4.3).

steps.action: Measure text over images, gradients and translucent overlays.
steps.expect: The ratio holds against the actual rendered background, at every scroll position where the text moves over different pixels.

steps.action: Measure UI component boundaries, focus indicators, icons carrying meaning, and chart elements.
steps.expect: Non-text elements needed to understand or operate the interface meet 3:1 (1.4.11).

plans.title: Zoom, reflow, text spacing and orientation
plans.why_manual: Every one of these is about what happens to a RENDERED layout under manipulation. 1.4.10, 1.4.13 and the reflow behaviour have no axe rule; jsdom cannot answer any of them because it has no layout engine.
preconditions: Record the exact viewport size and zoom level for each observation.

steps.action: Zoom text to 200% without zooming the page.
steps.expect: All content and functionality remain available with no loss (1.4.4).

steps.action: Set the viewport to 320 CSS pixels wide (or 400% zoom at 1280px).
steps.expect: Content reflows into one column with no two-dimensional scrolling, except for content that genuinely requires it such as a data table (1.4.10).

steps.action: Apply the 1.4.12 text-spacing overrides — line height 1.5×, paragraph spacing 2×, letter spacing 0.12em, word spacing 0.16em.
steps.expect: No content is clipped, overlapped or lost (1.4.12).

steps.action: Rotate a tablet or phone between portrait and landscape.
steps.expect: The interface works in both unless a specific orientation is essential (1.3.4).

plans.title: Images of text
plans.why_manual: No axe rule. Recognising that a picture contains text requires looking at it.
preconditions: Inventory images that render words: banners, diagrams, screenshots, logos.

steps.action: For each image containing text, ask whether real text could achieve the same presentation.
steps.expect: Text is used rather than an image of text, except for logotypes and cases where a particular presentation is essential (1.4.5).

steps.action: Zoom each such image to 200%.
steps.expect: Any text that remains as an image stays legible when magnified.

plans.title: Content revealed on hover or focus
plans.why_manual: No axe rule. Dismissible, hoverable and persistent are behaviours over time; they can only be observed by interacting.
preconditions: Inventory every tooltip, popover and hover card.

steps.action: Trigger each on hover, then press Escape.
steps.expect: It can be dismissed without moving the pointer or focus (dismissible).

steps.action: Move the pointer from the trigger onto the revealed content.
steps.expect: The content stays visible while the pointer is over it (hoverable).

steps.action: Leave the pointer on the trigger and wait.
steps.expect: The content remains until dismissed, focus moves away, or it stops being valid — it does not disappear on a timer (persistent).

steps.action: Repeat the whole plan using only the keyboard.
steps.expect: The same three behaviours hold when the content is revealed by focus.

plans.title: Content that starts, moves or flashes on its own
plans.why_manual: These share one test session: find everything that begins without the user asking, then verify it can be stopped. 2.3.1 has no axe rule, and a flash rate cannot be judged from markup.
preconditions: Inventory anything that autoplays, animates, scrolls, blinks or auto-updates, including carousels, toasts and live-updating counts.

steps.action: Load each screen and listen for audio that starts on its own.
steps.expect: Any audio playing longer than 3 seconds can be paused, stopped, or its volume controlled independently of the system volume (1.4.2).

steps.action: Watch each moving, blinking, scrolling or auto-updating element for more than 5 seconds.
steps.expect: A mechanism exists to pause, stop or hide it, unless it is essential (2.2.2).

steps.action: Observe anything that flashes.
steps.expect: Nothing flashes more than three times per second, or it stays below the general and red flash thresholds (2.3.1).

plans.title: Time limits are adjustable
plans.why_manual: axe can see a meta refresh. It cannot see a session timeout, an idle logout, or a form that expires server-side — which is where a real application's time limits live.
preconditions: Identify every time limit: session expiry, idle logout, auto-save windows, one-time codes, rate limits that discard work.

steps.action: Let a session reach its idle limit while a form is partly filled.
steps.expect: The user is warned with at least 20 seconds to extend, and can extend with a simple action (2.2.1).

steps.action: Extend the limit when prompted.
steps.expect: The limit extends at least ten times, and entered data survives.

steps.action: Check whether the limit can be turned off or lengthened to ten times the default in settings.
steps.expect: One of turn-off, adjust, or extend is available — or the limit is essential and documented as such.

plans.title: Pointer gestures, cancellation, motion and target size
plans.why_manual: Four of these five have no axe rule. Gestures, drag operations and device motion are input behaviours; only 2.5.8 target size is partly measurable from geometry.
preconditions: Use a real touch device for the gesture and motion steps.
Inventory every drag, swipe, pinch and multi-point interaction.

steps.action: For each path-based or multipoint gesture, look for a single-pointer alternative.
steps.expect: A single-tap, click or keyboard alternative exists unless the gesture is essential (2.5.1).

steps.action: Press down on a control, move the pointer away, and release.
steps.expect: The action does not fire on down-event, and can be aborted or undone (2.5.2).

steps.action: For each drag operation, attempt the same result without dragging.
steps.expect: A single-pointer alternative exists unless dragging is essential (2.5.7).

steps.action: Shake, tilt or move the device where motion triggers anything.
steps.expect: The function is also available through the interface, and motion actuation can be disabled (2.5.4).

steps.action: Measure the smallest interactive targets, including inline links in toolbars and icon buttons.
steps.expect: Targets are at least 24×24 CSS pixels, or spaced so a 24px circle does not overlap another target, or meet a listed exception (2.5.8).

plans.title: Page titles, link purpose and multiple ways
plans.why_manual: axe checks that a <title> EXISTS and that a link has SOME text. Whether the title describes the page, and whether the link text describes where it goes, are judgements about words. 2.4.5 has no axe rule.
preconditions: Work from a list of every distinct view in the product.

steps.action: Read each view's browser tab title.
steps.expect: It describes the topic or purpose of that view and distinguishes it from the others (2.4.2).

steps.action: Read every link's text out of context, then in context.
steps.expect: The purpose is determinable from the link text with its context (2.4.4).

steps.action: Count the ways to reach each view.
steps.expect: At least two independent ways exist — navigation, search, sitemap, in-context link — unless the view is a step in a process (2.4.5).

plans.title: Language of page and of parts
plans.why_manual: axe checks that `lang` is PRESENT and well formed. Whether the declared language is the language actually used, and whether foreign-language passages are marked, needs someone who can read the content.
preconditions: Include any localised builds in scope.

steps.action: Compare each page's declared lang against the language of its content.
steps.expect: The declared language is the one actually used (3.1.1).

steps.action: Find passages in a different language from the page.
steps.expect: Each is marked with its own lang, except proper names and technical terms (3.1.2).

steps.action: Listen to a mixed-language page with a screen reader.
steps.expect: Pronunciation switches at the marked passages.

plans.title: Predictable behaviour and consistency across views
plans.why_manual: None of these five has an axe rule, and none is a property of a single page — they compare behaviour ACROSS views, which is a session a person runs.
preconditions: Visit at least three views that share navigation and repeated controls.

steps.action: Tab onto every control without activating it.
steps.expect: Receiving focus alone never changes context — no navigation, no submission, no new window (3.2.1).

steps.action: Change every input's value: type, select, check, toggle.
steps.expect: Changing a setting alone never changes context without warning (3.2.2).

steps.action: Compare navigation across views.
steps.expect: Repeated navigation appears in the same relative order (3.2.3).

steps.action: Compare repeated icons, controls and labels across views.
steps.expect: Components with the same function are identified consistently (3.2.4).

steps.action: Locate the help mechanism on each view that offers one.
steps.expect: Help appears in the same relative order across views (3.2.6).

plans.title: Errors, error prevention, redundant entry and authentication
plans.why_manual: Four of these five have no axe rule. Every one is about what happens AFTER the user acts — submitting bad data, correcting it, re-entering it, or proving who they are.
preconditions: Identify forms that are legal, financial, or modify user-controlled data.
Have the sign-in flow available, including any second factor.

steps.action: Submit each form with invalid and missing values.
steps.expect: The field in error is identified in text, not by colour or position alone (3.3.1), and is announced by the screen reader.

steps.action: Read each error message.
steps.expect: It suggests how to correct the problem where the correction is known (3.3.3).

steps.action: Complete a legal, financial or data-modifying submission.
steps.expect: It is reversible, checked for errors with a chance to correct, or confirmed before finalising (3.3.4).

steps.action: Work through a multi-step flow that asks for the same information twice.
steps.expect: Previously entered information is auto-populated or selectable, unless re-entry is essential (3.3.7).

steps.action: Sign in, including any second factor.
steps.expect: No step requires a cognitive function test such as remembering or transcribing, or an alternative exists — and pasting into the password and code fields works (3.3.8).

plans.title: Identify input purpose
plans.why_manual: axe checks that an autocomplete token is VALID. Whether the right token was chosen for what the field collects — and whether a field collecting user information has one at all — is a judgement about the field's meaning.
preconditions: List every field that collects information ABOUT THE USER.

steps.action: For each such field, inspect its autocomplete attribute.
steps.expect: It carries the correct token from the HTML autofill list (1.3.5).

steps.action: Use the browser's own autofill on the form.
steps.expect: Values land in the fields they belong to.

steps.action: Check fields that do NOT collect user information.
steps.expect: They are not given a token that misdescribes them.
